text:
elyse - Support: escalating from customer acme-prodops — reported p95/p99 jump for streaming responses since last deploy, non-streaming calls unaffected. seeing TTFB stays low but total time spikes. case: #C-4812
vikram - Oncall: got it. any trace ids or example requests?
acme-prodops: sending one sample now — trace=trace-0a1b2c3d, route=/v1/chat/stream, model=redwood-open-7b, tokens=512. p99 ~2.4s, baseline ~350ms.
elyse - Support: attaching customer logs and patchy packet capture. They said it started after the 02:13 deploy last night.
deploy-bot: deploy finished: service=runtime, sha=3f7d9a2, env=prod, ts=1729964400
jamie - Runtime Eng: thanks — looking at traces. initial chunk flush looks normal but we're seeing extra wait between chunk 1 and chunk 2 (~1.6s) for this route. non-stream path pipelines the whole response in ~400ms.
kevin - SRE: any proxy or client differences? customer is using SSE via our edge in us-west2.
jamie - Runtime Eng: edge h2->sse translation is fine. hypothesis: sequence-number reorder or missing ack leading to retransmit/flush fallback in runtime. I can repro locally with a narrow timing window.
acme-prodops: can reproduce consistently on their side by sending 2 concurrent streams from same connection, otherwise intermittent.
elyse - Support: steps from customer to reproduce: 1) open SSE stream, 2) send prompt A (short), 3) immediately send prompt B on same connection, 4) observe first prompt responds fast, second stalls ~1.5-2s.
vikram - Oncall: thanks. can you paste a minimal curl for repro?
jamie - Runtime Eng: curl example to reproduce (SSE client):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-open-7b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"stream":true}' 
```
Then quickly send a second POST over same keep-alive connection.
kevin - SRE: I'm pulling kernel/tcp metrics and nginx proxy logs for that connection window. small chance of TCP write coalescing causing server-side backpressure.
jamie - Runtime Eng: also instrumented the runtime: I see our streaming flush heuristic defers chunk flush when sequence numbers appear out of order to preserve ordering; fallback path reserializes which adds 1-2s under burst. looks like sequence-number gaps are produced by our multiplexer when multiplexing concurrent streams.
elyse - Support: customer is asking for mitigation now (they're on a PLG tier).
vikram - Oncall: immediate mitigations: 1) suggest customer switch to non-streaming API for critical paths until we have a fix; 2) enable streaming_fallback_immediate=true for their tenant to avoid deferred flush; 3) temporary canary rollback of runtime sha 3f7d9a2 if rollback window open. Which is fastest?
jamie - Runtime Eng: fastest is tenant config toggle. I can flip it for acme-prodops now — it forces immediate chunk flush on any sequence anomaly (reduces extra delay at cost of potential out-of-order risk which is low for their usage).
kevin - SRE: I'll prepare rollback plan if toggle not acceptable. rollback would restore previous behavior before 02:13 deploy.
acme-prodops: prefer toggle first, will test and report. also curious about long-term fix.
jamie - Runtime Eng: long-term: fix multiplexer sequence assignment to avoid gaps and improve unit tests for concurrent streams; add a telemetry counter for 'seq-gap-fallback' and alert at p99 delta > 200ms.
vikram - Oncall: action items
- jamie: flip tenant config for acme-prodops and monitor (ETA 10m)
- kevin: collect full proxy+kernel logs from 02:00-03:00 UTC window and keep for postmortem (ETA 30m)
- elyse: coordinate with customer for immediate verification and capture additional traces (ETA 15m)
- jamie: open linted PR for sequence fix + add telemetry counter (ETA EOD)

jamie - Runtime Eng: toggled streaming_fallback_immediate for tenant=acme-prodops. watch their traces.
acme-prodops: just tested — second stream now responds inline, p99 dropped back to ~380ms. thank you! :tada:
elyse - Support: marking mitigation successful for now. will keep thread open until we ship a permanent fix.
kevin - SRE: grabbing logs now.
vikram - Oncall: good triage. add to incident board if regression rate > 5 tenants. jamie please raise an alert for seq-gap-fallback counter.
jamie - Runtime Eng: will add alert and PR linked to this thread. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/842
elyse - Support: documenting customer workaround in knowledge base: "Streaming: tenant toggle to force immediate flush on sequence anomalies" and linking case #C-4812.
acme-prodops: appreciate the quick help. keep us posted.
deploy-bot: scheduled-cadence: next deploy window 1729999999
vikram - Oncall: closing interim escalation — leave thread open for follow-ups.
